title: generativeaimarketingtradeoffs
claim: Generative AI marketing creates bland copy because teams prompt for personality instead of business trade-offs.
hook: Most generative AI marketing output sounds identical because teams prompt for tone instead of business constraints.

reel_script.onscreen: Generative AI marketing makes brands identical.
reel_script.voiceover: Generative AI marketing is causing a massive positioning problem across brands right now.
reel_script.direction: Rachit speaking directly to camera in studio.

reel_script.onscreen: You prompt for tone, not trade-offs.
reel_script.voiceover: Most marketing teams prompt language models by giving them a persona and a preferred tone of voice.

reel_script.onscreen: LLMs default to average market consensus.
reel_script.voiceover: Language models are statistical engines trained on the average of the internet. Prompt for tone, and you get average corporate fluff.
reel_script.direction: Medium shot with subtle graphic overlay of text lines.

reel_script.voiceover: To get sharp outputs, feed the model your business constraints instead: what your brand explicitly refuses to do.

reel_script.onscreen: Define exact pricing and speed trade-offs.
reel_script.voiceover: Tell the model: we cost thirty percent more, we take twice as long, and we do not offer customized plans.
Now the model stops trying to please everyone and writes from an actual strategic position.

reel_script.onscreen: Editorial edit time drops by 60 percent.
reel_script.voiceover: We tested this on three client briefs. Rewrites dropped from four rounds down to a single pass.

reel_script.onscreen: Send this to your brand manager.
reel_script.voiceover: Forward this to your content lead before they set up your next messaging workflow.

caption:
Most generative AI marketing output sounds identical because teams prompt for tone instead of business constraints.

When you tell a language model to sound professional, friendly, and premium, it calculates the statistical average of those words across billions of web pages. The result is generic copy that says nothing.

Positioning requires sacrifice. If you want AI tools to output usable brand messaging, you must feed them hard operational trade-offs:

1. What product features you deliberately lack
2. Which customer segments you choose to ignore
3. Where your pricing sits relative to competitors

AI does not lack creativity. Marketing teams lack clear positioning strategy to constrain it.

Send this to your brand manager before your next messaging sprint.

failure_mode: The advice could be mistaken for basic prompt engineering rather than a strategic commentary on positioning and business trade-offs.
